harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Built the double-NAT path across the 4-node cluster: node3 (lan-a, RHEL) -> node1 (VyOS, SNAT #1 on transit egress) -> node2 (OPNsense, SNAT #2 on lan-b egress) -> node4 (lan-b, RHEL, serving HTTP on :8080). Verified node4 records connections as arriving from node2's lan-b IP (10.10.3.254), not node3 or node1. All 4 nodes were restarted one at a time using their native reboot mechanisms, boot identity changes were proven, and full config/service/NAT persistence plus the double-NAT behavior were reconfirmed after each restart.
actions_performed: Discovered actual physical topology (node1 eth1/eth2 <-> node2 vtnet1/vtnet2 <-> node3/node4 enp8s0) via ip/ifconfig/arping/tcpdump, correcting an initial wrong NIC-to-link assumption on node1 by testing ARP reachability
Configured VyOS node1: eth2=10.10.1.254/24 (lan-a), eth1=10.10.2.1/24 (transit), NAT source rule 10 masquerading 10.10.1.0/24 to 10.10.2.1 on eth1 egress, static route 10.10.3.0/24 via 10.10.2.2

Configured OPNsense node2 via config.xml surgery + configctl: opt1=vtnet1=10.10.2.2/24 (transit), opt2=vtnet2=10.10.3.254/24 (lan-b), hybrid-mode outbound NAT rule SNATing 10.10.2.0/24 to the opt2 interface address, plus pass filter rules on opt1/opt2
Assigned static IPs via nmcli on node3 (10.10.1.10/24 + route to 10.10.3.0/24 via 10.10.1.254) and node4 (10.10.3.10/24)
Deployed a persistent systemd HTTP service (simple-http.service) on node4 listening on 0.0.0.0:8080, opened RHEL firewalld port 8080

Verified end-to-end curl from node3 to node4:8080 succeeds, and cross-checked both NAT hops via VyOS 'show nat source rules' and OPNsense 'pfctl -s states' showing the chain 10.10.1.x -> 10.10.2.1 -> 10.10.3.254 -> node4:8080

Captured boot_id/boottime baseline on all 4 nodes, restarted each node one at a time (native reboot: VyOS /sbin/reboot, FreeBSD /sbin/reboot, RHEL systemctl reboot), polled until exec was available again, confirmed changed boot identity, and reconfirmed interfaces/NAT/filter/service/route persistence and the working double-NAT connection after each restart

evidence.requirement: Baseline topology discovery and NIC-to-link mapping
evidence.summary: Established each node's OS/image (VyOS, OPNsense, RHEL10 x2) and enumerated all NICs including unconfigured secondary interfaces

evidence.requirement: Corrected wrong initial NIC pairing via ARP/tcpdump evidence
evidence.summary: arping from node3 failed on assumed eth1 link; tcpdump on node1 eth2 showed the actual ARP requests, proving node3 is wired to node1 eth2 not eth1, and the config was corrected accordingly

evidence.requirement: VyOS node1 SNAT #1 (lan-a source translated as it enters transit) configured and verified
evidence.summary: VyOS nat source rule 10 masquerades 10.10.1.0/24 to 10.10.2.1 on eth1 (transit) egress; show nat source rules confirms rule active; ping confirms transit link up

evidence.requirement: OPNsense node2 SNAT #2 (transit source translated as it enters lan-b) configured and verified
evidence.summary: config.xml surgery added opt1/opt2 interfaces and a hybrid-mode outbound NAT rule; configctl filter reload applied it; pfctl -s nat/rules shows 'nat on vtnet2 ... from 10.10.2.0/24 to any -> (vtnet2:0)' and pass rules on vtnet1/vtnet2

evidence.requirement: node4 records connection source as node2's lan-b address (10.10.3.254), not node3 or node1
evidence.summary: curl from node3 to node4:8080 succeeded; node4's HTTP access log shows client IP 10.10.3.254; OPNsense pf state table shows the double translation 10.10.2.1 -> 10.10.3.254 -> 10.10.3.10:8080

evidence.requirement: node1 healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 7668189d... and confirmed interfaces/NAT/route/ip_forward all correct prior to reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and post-restart recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; exec timed out during reboot; boot_id changed to 637ca974...; interfaces/NAT/static route/ip_forward all confirmed restored

evidence.requirement: node2 healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured kern.boottime (05:14:41) and confirmed vtnet1/vtnet2 NAT+filter rules active prior to reboot

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and post-restart recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged; SSH connection timed out during reboot; kern.boottime changed to 05:23:21; vtnet1 (10.10.2.2) and vtnet2 (10.10.3.254) confirmed restored with correct descriptions/IPs

evidence.requirement: node3 healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id aad96cc9... prior to reboot

evidence.requirement: node3 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and post-restart recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged; exec timed out during reboot; boot_id changed to 65e1f53f...; enp8s0 static IP and route restored, and curl to node4:8080 succeeded again post-restart

evidence.requirement: node4 healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 739c9792... and confirmed simple-http.service active and listening on 8080 prior to reboot

evidence.requirement: node4 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and post-restart recovery with re-verified double-NAT behavior
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged; exec timed out during reboot; boot_id changed to 336bb0d1...; enp8s0 IP and simple-http.service (auto-started) confirmed restored; final curl from node3 succeeded and node4's access log shows source 10.10.3.254, confirming the double-NAT chain survived all four restarts
